Follow up in 1 week to lock timeline and pilot scope

meeting_header: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC | 45 minutes | Attendees: Samir Patel, Lena Ortiz (Redwood), Carlos Mendoza, Priya Singh, Dana Park (Odyssey Labs)
summary: Initial discovery for migrating Odyssey Labs from OpenAI-hosted models to Redwood Dedicated. Key topics: API compatibility, model/eval parity, performance (vLLM/TGI), security (SOC2/KMS/VPC), sizing and pricing. Agreed to run benchmarks with customer prompt sets and share pricing/security docs.
topics: Migration path from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated
Compatibility for prompts, function calling, and tokenization
Performance: vLLM & TGI parity and KV cache behavior
Security requirements: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, network/VPC
Sizing and pricing for Dedicated capacity
transcript: 00:00 - Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir, account exec on Redwood. With me is Lena from our solutions team. How's everyone doing?

00:12 - Carlos Mendoza: Good, thanks. Carlos here, CTO at Odyssey. We wanted to kick off the migration convo mostly from OpenAI hosted to a Dedicated instance. We have some performance and cost concerns.
00:28 - Priya Singh: Hi all, Priya. I own the ML infra and will run the benchmarks. We're using a mix of gpt-4 style prompts and some retrieval-augmented generation with long contexts.

00:40 - Samir Patel: Great context. High-level, we help with hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Today we'll focus on Dedicated migration path and what parity looks like vs OpenAI function calls, streaming, prompt behavior, etc.

01:05 - Lena Ortiz: Quick note  we often see customers care about two things: functional parity (does the output match) and performance/cost. We try to map both. Can you describe current traffic and SLOs?

01:20 - Dana Park: We average about 150 QPS at peak for short-chat flows, and up to 40 concurrent long-context RAG sessions latency target sub-500ms for short responses. Cost with OpenAI is getting high, so we're exploring Dedicated to control unit economics.

01:45 - Samir Patel: Understood. On Dedicated you get reserved GPU pools predictable throughput and lower per-token cost. We also support auto-scaling policies and burst options. For RAG long contexts, we recommend KV caching + continuous batching to keep latency down.
02:10 - Carlos Mendoza: Two immediate questions: 1) How compatible is Redwood with OpenAI APIs? 2) If we run our eval suite, will outputs be identical or do we expect diffs?

02:25 - Lena Ortiz: Good questions. For compatibility we provide OpenAI-like endpoints and SDKs for many models, but there are differences: tokenization, temperature sampling, and occasional function-calling semantics. We aim for high parity but not byte-for-byte identical. Our process is to run evals and flag regressions.
02:50 - Priya Singh: When you say function-calling differences like tools and structured responses how big are those? We rely on deterministic JSON outputs from functions for downstream parsing.

03:05 - Lena Ortiz: The function-calling primitives are supported, but nuance exists around completion truncation and how the model chooses function vs text. We can tune system prompts and use our structured output helpers to increase determinism. For mission-critical parsing we recommend a small wrapper validation step in your pipeline.
03:30 - Dana Park: About the runtime we have been reading about vLLM and TGI. Are those part of Redwood's stack or do we need to run them ourselves?

03:45 - Samir Patel: Redwood's serving runtime supports models that customers often run on vLLM/TGI, but we manage the inference engine on our Dedicated nodes. We do kernel selection and some compilation. If you have a custom vLLM build, there are paths to bring it, but typical migrations use our curated images which are tuned for throughput and latency.
04:10 - Carlos Mendoza: Ok. For our eval parity we run automated BLEU/ROUGE and human evals. What's the best way to validate outputs during migration?

04:25 - Lena Ortiz: We suggest three stages: 1) offline eval: run your prompt suite through Redwood Dedicated in a staging cluster; 2) A/B rollout: canary some traffic with fallback to OpenAI; 3) human spot checks. We'll provide a benchmark harness and help run the vLLM/TGI parity tests.
04:50 - Priya Singh: Does Redwood preserve the same tokenizer / token counts? Our billing and prompt truncation logic depends on token counts matching OpenAI's counts closely.

05:05 - Samir Patel: Tokenization can differ slightly across model implementations. We provide tokenization tools and token-count mapping guidance. In practice most customers see small variances; we recommend using our tokenization library during migration and adapt billing thresholds if needed.
05:30 - Dana Park: Security is key: SOC 2 type II, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS integration, and VPC peering or Private link. What's supported on Dedicated?

05:45 - Lena Ortiz: Dedicated supports private control planes, VPC peering, customer-managed KMS/HSM, SSO via SAML/Okta, RBAC, and detailed audit logs. We'll share the security whitepaper and network diagram. We also have an enterprise package for longer log retention and compliance add-ons.
06:10 - Carlos Mendoza: Good. One concern: can we bring our own model weights (licensed) and run them on Redwood Dedicated or is it only curated models?

06:25 - Samir Patel: We support bringing your own models in Private deployments and on some Dedicated plans there are licensing and ops considerations. For curated open models we provide verified performance profiles. If you have licensed weights we can discuss governance and operational handoffs.
06:45 - Priya Singh: About throughput we need consistent 150 QPS with <500ms p50. What GPU types and node sizing do you recommend?

07:00 - Lena Ortiz: For chat-like 8k context workloads, we typically suggest an A100-style pod configuration with 2-4 GPUs per pool depending on batching behavior. We'll run your prompt set and tune batch sizes and quantization settings. The Dedicated sizing worksheet will show modeled throughput for your mix.
07:30 - Dana Park: Any gotchas on autoscaling? We need predictable tail latency during bursts.

07:45 - Samir Patel: Autoscaling is policy-driven and includes surge capacity options. For tight p99 SLAs we recommend some reserved headroom and a fast warmup path (hot model replicas + KV cache priming). Redwood also supports fallback policies to smaller but faster model variants for graceful degradation.
08:10 - Carlos Mendoza: How do you handle data residency? We process EU customer data and have regional constraints.

08:20 - Lena Ortiz: Dedicated can be provisioned in specific cloud regions and we support Private deployments for strict residency. We also support customer-managed keys and can sign BAA/DPAs as needed.
08:40 - Priya Singh: Performance question vLLM claims big gains with sequence parallelism. Are your benchmarks comparable? We currently run vLLM on-prem for a subset of models.

08:55 - Samir Patel: We benchmark against vLLM and TGI setups. Our runtime includes optimizations (KV cache management, continuous batching, custom kernels) that yield comparable or better p50/p95 in many workloads. We'll run your vLLM-configured prompts to compare.
09:15 - Dana Park: For our POC we'd like a two-week pilot on Dedicated with access to performance metrics and billing telemetry. Is that a normal path?

09:28 - Lena Ortiz: Yes most customers do a pilot. For Dedicated pilots we provision a smaller reserved pool, run benchmark workloads, and provide the console access with per-route cost/latency breakdowns. That will help you model unit economics.
09:50 - Carlos Mendoza: About API changes do we need to retrain any of our prompt tuning or RLHF wrappers? We want to avoid a big rework.

10:05 - Samir Patel: Usually prompt knobs transfer well but we do see some delta. For critical RLHF or tuned prompts, customers run a lightweight re-eval and sometimes small prompt adjustments. Our optimize tooling can recommend quantization and batching profiles while minimizing quality regressions.
10:30 - Priya Singh: Can we do canary routing some percentage to Redwood Dedicated, rest to OpenAI?
10:40 - Lena Ortiz: Absolutely. Smart routing supports canary/A-B and automatic fallback policies. You can split by route, model, or latency threshold.
11:00 - Dana Park: Pricing what's the typical committed cost vs our current OpenAI spend?

11:10 - Samir Patel: It depends on committed throughput and storage. Generally customers see 30-60% reduction in per-token cost when moving to Dedicated if utilization is decent. We'll send a sizing and pricing worksheet with modeled costs based on your QPS and prompt lengths.

11:35 - Carlos Mendoza: For the benchmark, we'll share three prompt sets: short chat, long RAG, structured function-calls. Priya will drop them into the repo. We expect the benchmarks to be fairly deterministic.
11:50 - Priya Singh: I'll drop the prompt sets and expected QPS into the shared folder by Friday. Also flagging we use a custom tokenizer endpoint we'll include tokenization samples.

12:05 - Lena Ortiz: Perfect. We'll use those to run the vLLM/TGI parity runs and produce a diff report (automated metrics + sample mismatches). Expect the initial report in ~5 business days after we get the prompts.

12:25 - Samir Patel: Quick note on logs and observability: you'll get per-request traces, token-level cost, and model-level dashboards. We can hook to your existing observability stack via exporters if needed.
12:45 - Dana Park: Ops question who owns upgrades and kernel patches on Dedicated? We need an SLA for maintenance windows.

12:55 - Lena Ortiz: Redwood manages the runtime stack for Dedicated with optional maintenance windows. For Private/on-prem we offer the bundle but customer ops may control upgrade cadence. We'll include maintenance SLAs in the enterprise addendum.
13:15 - Carlos Mendoza: Any sample artifacts you'd share now?

13:20 - Samir Patel: I'll send: pricing_sheet_v2.xlsx, security_whitepaper.pdf, network_diagram.png and a link to the benchmark harness repo. I'll put them in the shared drive link: https://redwood.app/odyssey/shared (note: placeholder)
13:40 - Priya Singh: Good. Also can we get tokenization and exact model config (temperature, top_p defaults) used by Redwood for parity runs?
13:55 - Lena Ortiz: Yes, we'll include default runtime config and the tokenization library. We'll also document differences in sampling seeds and suggested guardrails for deterministic outputs.
14:10 - Dana Park: Timeline: if we start pilot next week how long to be production-ready?

14:18 - Samir Patel: Typical path is 2–4 weeks for pilot + benchmark, then 4–8 weeks for production rollout depending on integration depth. For you, with the eval suite and prompt sets, we can accelerate parts of it.
14:35 - Carlos Mendoza: Ok that sounds reasonable. Any legal/procurement items to start for procurement?
14:42 - Samir Patel: We'll share master service agreement, order form examples, and the SOC2 report. Procurement can review while we run the pilot.
14:58 - Priya Singh: Quick nit: when you said fallback to smaller variants — is there an automatic fallback mapping or we need to define routes?
15:08 - Lena Ortiz: There are pre-configured policies we can use and you can customize per-route fallbacks. We'll sample suggestions based on your latency/cost SLOs.

15:25 - Samir Patel: Wrapping up — recap of next steps: Samir send pricing and security docs; Priya share prompt sets + tokenization samples; Lena prep benchmark harness and schedule pilot; meet again in one week to review results.
15:45 - Carlos Mendoza: Thanks everyone. We'll get the artifacts over and look forward to the benchmark.
15:54 - Dana Park: Thanks, bye.
15:58 - Samir Patel: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email with links and dates.
